title: Design System: Bootlegger — Orchard Park Night

display.purpose: Anton: the BOOTLEGGER wordmark (italic, Bills-red drop shadow) and room/plate titles.

body.purpose: Barlow Semi Condensed: prose, labels, tabs, buttons; also the legibility floor for the smallest, densest labels.

figures.purpose: Courier Prime, every number always (the Typewriter Figures Rule); ledger, tape, stepper, and clock text ride along; 700 marks the emphasized figure.

banner.purpose: Permanent Marker, memes only: the Mafia stamps and THE TABLE's FOLDED tag. Never data, labels, or controls (the Bedsheet Marker Rule).

shadows.name: plate
shadows.purpose: --shadow-plate: the loud objects (masthead, The Call, verdict).

shadows.name: paper-drop
shadows.purpose: Program sheets float highest; the inset is floodlight catching the paper's top edge.

shadows.name: paper-drop-tape
shadows.purpose: Shallower drop for the pick ticker tape.

shadows.name: glow-royal-plate
shadows.purpose: Clockplate when you're on the clock — royal glow means yours/act.

shadows.name: glow-royal-key
shadows.purpose: Primary button: the hard 3px press edge plus royal underglow; active collapses to 0 1px 0 #0a1c44 with translateY(2px).

shadows.name: glow-lamp-dot
shadows.purpose: Wire-live lamp dot; swaps to rgba(255,93,102,.8) when the wire is down.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: The house spring — rows, strike, settle, and the tag slam all ride it.

motion.name: room-in
motion.purpose: The broadcast cut: rooms, verdict, sheets, report card, deals rise and settle. Keys off the [hidden] display restart, so 1 Hz polls never re-fire it.

motion.name: row-in
motion.value: row-in .28s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both; 30ms stagger, capped at 180ms from nth-child(7)
motion.purpose: Board rows cascade on rebuild only; transform/opacity only.

motion.name: strike
motion.value: strike .5s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both (scaleX 0→1 at -1.1deg, origin left center)
motion.purpose: The pick strike draws left-to-right through the name. Off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: The pick stamp slams and settles; .just-picked held 1.4s by JS. Off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: buf-idle
motion.purpose: The Buffalo's breathing bob on The Call; the static mascot remains under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: buf-stampede
motion.purpose: On your clock the Buffalo stampedes across the plate twice; dust is display:none under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: run-route
motion.purpose: The telestrator's royal pen draws the route on loop; display:none under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: hurdle
motion.value: hurdle 1s cubic-bezier(.3,.1,.5,1) both (2.5 turns, up and over the row)
motion.purpose: Your landed pick's football flyby; display:none under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: tag-slam
motion.purpose: THE TABLE's FOLDED tag and the mafia-stamp slam; renders instantly under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: toggle
motion.purpose: Program-sheet toggle track/knob; off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: 12px in-button spinner; slowed to 1.5s (not removed) under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.northStar: A Bills Night Game as a Working Interface
narrative.overview:
ORCHARD PARK NIGHT: a Bills night game rendered as a broadcast-grade board, never a costume of team logos. Deep stadium navy carries the working surfaces, with faint yard lines and hash ticks drawn into the ground itself and grain over everything; white ink does the reading. Electric royal is the voice of everything you can touch — tabs, the primary key, focus rings, your rows, the burning survival track — and Bills red is reserved strictly for trouble. The fandom lives in a strictly rationed meme layer: one authored zubaz stripe, a cartoon buffalo on The Call, a folding table beside the shelf, and bedsheet-marker stamps.

The second material is the white game program: the ledger, rules, ticker tape, and Scout's File print on cool white paper with a red ledger margin rule, carrying its own complete ink set. Numbers are the cargo and every one of them is typewriter type. The board is dense on purpose — read at a glance under a draft clock or before kickoff — so hierarchy does the work: tier bands, chalked survival meters, stamped picks, one loud royal-edged plate per room.

The web surface (server/app/web/) is the authority for this system; the draft-overlay extension (v1.4.0) and the Expo app's mobile/src/theme.ts mirror these tokens and must follow this file. In styles.css the variable names keep their old spellings (--brass = royal, --lamp = good, --marigold = warn, --oxblood = flag); the world they paint is this one.
keyCharacteristics: Two materials: stadium-navy working surfaces (with yard lines in the ground) and white game-program paper, each with its own complete ink set.
Royal is touchable; Bills red is trouble only; verified green is earned. The meme layer's red is fandom, not status.
One zubaz: an authored irregular red/royal tile worn only by the masthead and the report card.
Every figure is typewriter type (Courier Prime); Anton belongs to the wordmark and titles; Permanent Marker to the meme stamps alone.
A rationed fun layer — buffalo, telestrator, ball hurdle, THE TABLE — that reacts to real events and never talks over the figures.
One motion grammar (the broadcast cut): rise-settle entries keyed off [hidden] toggles, transform/opacity only, dead under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Typewriter Figures Rule
rules.body: If it is a number, it is Courier Prime — in tables, meters, stamps, steppers, clocks, and tape. UI labels around a figure stay in the condensed gothic, so figures always look typed onto the surface rather than styled.

rules.name: The Written Label Rule
rules.body: A position hue never appears without its written code beside it — the swatch-plus-text .pos tag is the only way position identity is drawn. Color alone identifies nothing, anywhere: injury, failure, and verification likewise always pair color with a word or icon.

rules.name: The Royal Is Touchable, Red Is Trouble Rule
rules.body: Royal marks the interactive world; Bills red marks trouble only — wire down, failed, hurt, struck through. The two semantics never blur. The meme layer's red (zubaz, wordmark drop shadow, bedsheet stamps) is fandom, not status: it never colors a figure, a label, or a control.

rules.name: The One Zubaz Rule
rules.body: The zubaz is an authored SVG tile of irregular hand-cut red/royal jags on white — real zebra print, not a candy stripe. Exactly two things wear it: the masthead strip and the report card headband. Nowhere else, ever.

rules.name: The Paper Ink Rule
rules.body: Program-paper surfaces carry their own ink tokens (paper-ink, paper-faint, paper-ok, paper-bad), each holding >=4.5:1 against the sheet gradient's darkest stop. Navy-surface inks never sit on paper; paper inks never sit on navy. Crossing a material means switching ink sets.

rules.name: The Bedsheet Marker Rule
rules.body: Permanent Marker appears only in the meme stamps — .mafia-stamp and THE TABLE's FOLDED tag. Never in data, labels, or controls. Anywhere else it is a defect.

rules.name: The No Sideways Page Rule
rules.body: The page never scrolls horizontally (body { overflow-x: clip }). Wide strips — the ticker tape, the stepper, the report card, the mobile tab row — scroll inside their own containers with material-matched scrollbars. On phones the stepper compresses rather than wraps.

rules.name: The Broadcast Cut Rule
rules.body: One motion grammar: rooms rise and settle in 200ms; rows cascade on a 30ms stagger capped at 180ms; transform/opacity only. Entries key off the [hidden] toggle's display restart, so tab switches and rebuilds animate and the 1 Hz poll patches never re-fire anything. prefers-reduced-motion strips the characters rather than freezing them: dust, telestrator, and flyby go display:none, the static buffalo stays, and the board reads perfectly as a still.

dos: Do pair every position hue with its written label and every status color with a word or icon — color alone carries no meaning anywhere.
Do set every number in Courier Prime — figures, stamps, timestamps, bids, percentages — with gothic micro-labels beside them.
Do keep royal for the interactive world and Bills red for trouble; a red button or a royal error state is a defect.
Do switch to the program-paper ink set the moment content sits on a sheet or tape, including selection, scrollbars, and focus rings.
Do keep approval actions at least 44px tall (46px built), full-width on the phone, with the hard 3px press edge.
Do make every degraded state visible and worded in the house voice — CIRCLE THE WAGONS with the data's age, never a silent stall.
Do key entry animations off [hidden] display restarts so polling never re-fires them; new motion is transform/opacity only.
donts: Don't put the zubaz anywhere but the masthead and the report card.
Don't set anything but the wordmark and room/plate titles in Anton, and nothing but meme stamps in Permanent Marker.
Don't use good/warn/flag as series, position, or decorative colors, or position hues as status colors.
Don't let the page scroll horizontally, ever — wide data scrolls inside its own container.
Don't put navy-surface inks or accents on program paper, or paper inks on navy — crossing materials means switching ink sets.
Don't drift toward the refused worlds: no white-card sports-app dashboard, no costume of team logos or licensed marks.
Don't add a character or theatrical animation beyond the built four (buffalo, telestrator, hurdle, THE TABLE); anything new must die under prefers-reduced-motion.
